findings.reason: the plan must state which way the unknown type goes (and cover it in the done-when's refusal list); as written the node implements an unspecified, untested path in the one guard whose whole purpose is refusing a shared mount for WAL.
findings.text: §5 refuses only types present in `_SHARED_FILESYSTEMS`, but `host._filesystem_type` returns `None` when `/proc/self/mountinfo` is unreadable (`reckon/host.py:168`–`169`), so an undeterminable type is accepted and the guard fails open exactly when it cannot prove the root is node-local

findings.reason: the two sections must agree on who owns the `cursors` table, or the sole-writer invariant §7 rests on is false and a node enforcing it would refuse the subscriber's write; the prior review never raised this.
findings.text: §7 states the station "is the database's only writer", but §8 has the subscriber "advance its cursor in the same transaction", and `cursors` is one of §5's own tables in that store (a second writer process on the node-local database)
